sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Kapil Kumar,Nitika Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.
Heard Sri Kapil Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Shashi Kant Pandey, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.

2. The present application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant Rohit with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 887 of 2021, under Sections 376, 511 I.P.C. and Section 6/18 POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Loni Border, District Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.
3. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 21.08.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.1821 of 2022 (Rohit vs. State of U.P. and 2 others).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that only ground which is being pressed, is regarding the period of detention.
It is submitted that the applicant is in jail since 04.10.2021 and the trial in the matter has not yet been concluded.
It is further submitted that till now only three witnesses have been examined before the trial court and as such trial will take time for its conclusion.
It is submitted that looking to the period of detention, the applicant be enlarged on bail.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that this is the second bail application of the applicant.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on merits vide order dated 21.08.2023.
It is submitted that the victim was examined as P.W.-2 before the trial court who has supported the prosecution case and has also stated that the applicant has committed rape upon her.
She also identified the accused present in the dock.
It is further submitted that there is no new and fresh ground in the present bail application.
The trial in the matter is going on in which three witnesses have been examined, hence the bail application be thus rejected.
6. After having heard the learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the The present bail application is the second bail application of the applicant.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected on merits vide order dated 14.12.2023.

The said order reads as under :-
"1. List revised.
2. Heard Sri Shyam Babu Vaish, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Virendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.
3.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Rohit, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 887 of 2021, under sections 376, 511 I.P.C. and section 6/18 POCSO Act, Police Station Loni Border, District Ghaziabad.
4. The F.I.R. of the present matter has been lodged by Santosh Maurya against the applicant alleging therein that his daughter aged about 8 years is a student of class IV.
On 03.10.2021 at about 4.00 P.M., she was going to purchase pencil and rubber from the shop of Saurabh situated near house.

On the way, the applicant forcibly pulled her daughter in the vegetable field and put out her clothes and also put out his clothes and tried to commit rape on which his daughter started weeping and crying and Imran, Sagar and Rahul reached there and by exercising extra force apprehended the applicant and got his daughter safe.
The applicant was then brought to the police station and a report was lodged.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the present case is a case of attempt to rape.
It is argued that the parents of the victim refused her medical examination.

While placing para 18 of the affidavit, learned counsel for the applicant has argued Rohit vs State Of U.P. & Others on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74530765/
2 that the applicant is mentally weak person.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 21 of the affidavit and he is in jail since 04.10.2021.

6. Per contra learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is named in the statements of victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and there is allegation against him.
Applicant was apprehended on the spot and was brought to the police station and handed over to the police.
It is argued that the victim is aged about 8 years and is a minor girl, thus the bail application of the applicant be rejected.
7. After hearing the counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is apparent that the victim is aged about 8 years.
The applicant was apprehended from the spot and brought to the police station.
Insofar as the ground of mentally illness is concerned the same is a matter of trial which needs evidence.
Victim has named the applicant and there are allegation against him.
No case for bail is made out against the applicant.
8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case for bail, hence, the bail application is rejected. "
7. The trial is under progress in which three witnesses have been examined.
The victim was examined as P.W.-2 who has supported the prosecution case and has stated that the applicant has committed rape upon her.
She identified the accused-applicant when he was present in court as an accused who committed rape upon her.
The trial in the matter is going on and it cannot be said that the applicant is in jail without the trial proceeding.
There is nothing credible to consider the second bail application of the applicant at this stage.
The same is thus rejected.
8. The second bail application is rejected.

(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 8.1.2025 / Manoj  Rohit vs State Of U.P. & Others on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74530765/
